portfolio.summary: The pilots are decisive: the forward model is exact, and both physics MLE and the hybrid reach about 0.019 rel_l2 at n=60, well under the 0.05 target and calibrated. Further debate will not change what is worth running. The full-val runs of P-009, P-010 and P-011 form a clean, paired 2x2-style decomposition: init vs none, mode vs mean. These should run first, with per-sample CRB, stratification by distance to bound and ESS logged. P-014 should fix its self-contradictory 5% criterion or merge into P-009 as an init variant. P-012 should be made conditional on P-010 finding basin failures. P-013 is cheap but needs an in-arm log-target twin and seed replication. Test-split use remains prohibited for selection; the final choice should be made on full-val paired comparisons.
portfolio.diversity_assessment: The portfolio is narrow. Four of six arms are log-LM physics/hybrids with minor variations in init or readout. P-013 is the only purely amortised arm. This narrowness is justified by the pilots: two n=60 pilots already sit at about the CRB, with calibrated chi2 and coverage, and forward consistency is verified. The remaining scientific questions are efficiency, basin failures and the MMSE edge effect, not method discovery. The total deterministic estimate is about 196 s of the 400 worker-second budget, so all arms fit. If budget pressure appears, P-012 and P-014 should be cut first.
missing_controls: Per-sample CRB at val truths, obtainable from the LM final Jacobian. Every efficiency and stratification criterion depends on it, yet all proposals use the 32-draw median.
A Bayesian (Van Trees) bound under the box prior. MMSE estimators can beat the frequentist CRB, so the 'CRB floor' framing is not a floor for P-009, P-011 or P-014.
Code check of whether posterior_mean averages in k or log k.

Seed variance for MLP arms (P-013), and IS precision matched across compared hybrids (P-012 at 64 vs P-009 at 256 samples).

unresolved: challenge: The prediction (<0.022) is weak given the pilot already gave 0.0186. A result of 0.021 would 'confirm' the hypothesis but would be an 13% regression from the pilot. Tighten it to a band, e.g. rel_l2 in [0.016, 0.021], or state the efficiency ratio rel_l2/CRB_val you expect.

challenge: The CRB reference 0.0186 comes from 32 prior draws, and it bounds unbiased estimators only. A box-prior posterior mean is biased and can legitimately go below the CRB, especially for k1 and k4 near bounds. 'Within 1.2x of the CRB' is therefore not an efficiency claim unless the CRB is recomputed per val sample. The relevant floor for an MMSE estimator is a Bayesian (Van Trees) bound.

challenge: The pilot P-001 label shows 'ridge/log+pca40', i.e. log features, with train_fraction=300. This proposal uses raw features and presumably the full train set. The init has changed, so the pilot is not strictly the same arm. Report init-only rel_l2 to show the change is harmless.

challenge: Criterion (b) uses 1.5x the CR std for k2 and k3 from the 32-draw median. Per-sample CR std varies with k, so an aggregate RMSE is being compared against a median std. Use the RMS of per-sample CR std over the val set instead.
